title: Pressure Type Variation on Open-Source vs. Closed-Source Models
original_idea: Apply the same sycophancy stress battery (emotional, authority, logical pressure types) to Llama 3.1, Mistral, Gemma, and Qwen model families. Compare against closed-source baselines.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Useful comparative data but the impact pathway is indirect. Informs model selection rather than directly improving safety mechanisms.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running multiple model families including open-source models locally. Medium compute helps but managing multiple model deployments adds complexity for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Testing across 4+ model families with multiple pressure types is broad. Hard to complete rigorously in 30hrs even with existing benchmarks.

novelty.reasoning: Sycophancy comparisons across model families exist but have not systematically compared open-source vs closed-source on matched pressure batteries. (1) SycEval (arXiv:2502.08177, 2025) benchmarks GPT-4, Gemini, and ChatGPT, finding overall 58.19% sycophancy with model-specific rates. (2) Various benchmarks (Syco-bench, ELEPHANT) test multiple models but do not frame the comparison as open-vs-closed. (3) Sycophancy scaling work compares within model families (PaLM, Llama) rather than across the open/closed divide. The specific framing of open-source vs closed-source as the key comparison variable, combined with pressure type interactions, adds a dimension not explicitly covered. However, the individual model results from existing benchmarks could be reassembled to partially answer this question.

evidence: ELEPHANT: Measuring and Understanding Social Sycophancy in LLMs. arXiv:2505.13995, 2025.
Sycophancy in Large Language Models: Causes and Mitigations. arXiv:2411.15287, 2024.
